segments.text: Today I want to talk about strength training after the age of forty.
Most people think cardio is the only way to lose weight, and that is simply not true.
Muscle burns more calories at rest than fat does.
I recommend lifting weights three times a week for forty-five minutes.
Start with compound lifts like squats, deadlifts, and bench press.
Protein matters a lot, so aim for about one point six grams per kilogram of body weight.
Sleep is when your body actually repairs the muscle you broke down in the gym.
If you sleep less than six hours, your cortisol goes up and your recovery goes down.
Don't chase the scale, because your weight can change by two pounds in a single day.
Take a progress photo every two weeks instead.
Walking ten thousand steps a day is a great baseline for heart health.
Creatine monohydrate, five grams a day, is one of the most studied supplements out there.
Drink water before every meal, and you will naturally eat less.
Consistency beats intensity every single time.
Small habits, repeated daily, change your body in six months.
Stop looking for the perfect program and just show up on Monday.
